title: Escalation stabilization: Safe Fastpass, retry-quarantine, and targeted patch for hosted 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: In response to multiple customer escalations during a tenant surge (manifesting as 5xx HTTP responses and increased request timeouts), this ticket captures a safe, low-risk stabilization path (Safe Fastpass + retry-quarantine) + a small targeted code patch to prevent retry amplification and long tail timeouts for streaming and batch requests.

Background: Over the last 48 hours we observed tenant-sourced request surges that triggered kernel backpressure and KV cache thrashing; the surface symptoms were: intermittent 502/503s from inference workers, long tail client timeouts, and cascading upstream retries that amplified load. Customers reported partial transcript drops and elevated latency. Several escalations requested immediate safeguards and a timeline for a permanent fix.

Goal: Deploy a short-lived mitigation that reduces customer-visible 5xx/timeouts within minutes, preserve availability for high-priority tenants, and implement a low-risk server-side patch that avoids altering model kernels or quantization paths. The mitigation must be rollback-safe and observable.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate a tenant burst by replaying a 10x qps workload against a single tenant id with a mix of streaming + short-text generation requests.
2) Observe edge proxy request queue growth (frontdoor) and increased connection hold time on fronting proxies.
3) Trigger inference worker KV cache compaction by sending many new prompt prefixes to force KV churn.
4) Watch downstream worker 5xx rate increase and client-side retries multiplying the effective QPS.
5) Correlate with traces (trace IDs included in attachments) to see inflight request queueing and retry storms.
mitigation_plan:
Phase A (immediate, non-invasive):
- Enable tenant-level retry-quarantine: temporarily cap automatic client-originated retries per tenant in the edge layer to 3 at 30s windows (config toggle).
- Activate Safe Fastpass routing for high-priority tenants: route requests for customers with active escalations to a reserved worker pool that applies strict admission and preemptive queueing.
- Shorten streaming idle timeout to 8s on frontdoor to surface backpressure earlier and avoid long-held connections.

Phase B (targeted code fix):
- Patch request fanout logic to prefer hedging over naive retries for long-running upstream calls (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128).
- Add guard in KV cache compaction code to avoid aggressive synchronous compaction during high insertion rates (commit: 7b9c3d4).
- Add metric: tenant_retry_amplification_ratio and alert threshold to paging channel.

Phase C (rollout + follow-up):
- Canary patch in staging then 10% of production traffic for 2h, monitor 5xx rate and retry amplification metric.
- If stable, ramp to 100% with 5-minute step increments.
- Postmortem and runbook updates after stabilization.
proposed_fix_summary: Small patch that changes retry/fanout orchestration: introduce a per-request hedging window (default 300ms) and a tenant-aware admission policy at the proxy. Prevent synchronous KV compaction while compaction_suppression flag is set when insertion rate > 5000/s. No model or kernel changes. Backwards-compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments via config toggles.
acceptance_criteria: 5xx rate attributable to the surge reduced by >= 80% for impacted tenants within 1 hour of deployment.
Retry amplification ratio metric decreases to below 1.5 for the incident tenant(s).
No regression in median latency for non-impacted tenants (> +/- 10%).
Canary rollout completes without new alerts for at least 1 hour at 10% traffic.
Runbook updated and customer comms drafted by SRE and Solutions teams.
